practice.foundation[2]: Label the axes Speed and Time. Correct the explanation: graph A also has continuous speed; its sharp minimum represents an abrupt change in acceleration, rather than an instantaneous speed jump.

practice.development[1]: Specify the variables represented by each graph, as the source does: Time horizontally, with water level, call cost or remaining wax vertically for the corresponding story.

practice.development[2]: The solution starts flat and initially increases at an increasing rate, contrary to both the question and source. Correct the plotted curve and explanation to show an initially rapid rise followed by a decreasing rate of increase.
practice.development[3]: The solution incorrectly starts the town's population at zero. Start above zero; the source also shows a positive initial population.

practice.development[4]: Explaining an error in a supplied student construction is not asked anywhere in the supplied section. Replace this item with an adapted Development graph-selection or scenario-sketching task and update its structure slug.

quiz.q1: Label the axes Height and Time.

quiz.q3: Label the axes Height and Time, and state that height is measured above the release-and-catch level, with the ball caught at its release height. Otherwise the plotted zero endpoints do not match ordinary height above ground.
quiz.q4: Label the axes Fatigue score and Distance.
quiz.q5: Label the axes Temperature and Time. Change the structure slug to scenario-to-graph because this task selects a supplied graph rather than sketching one.

quiz.q7: Label the axes Height and Time, and change the structure slug to scenario-to-graph.

quiz.q9: Label the axes Height and Time, and change the structure slug to container-to-graph: the requested task is graph selection. In A's explanation, distinguish the changing height-increase rate from the constant volume fill rate.

theory: A wide cross-section produces a shallow rising graph, not a flat graph; only unchanged height gives a horizontal segment. Replace the claim that a suddenly refilled tank undergoes a physically instantaneous height jump: refilling takes time and may instead appear as a steep rise at the chosen scale.
summary: Added the required axis labels, corrected the identified curves, initial populations, cooling level and explanations, and repaired theory wording and task slugs. Replaced the three unsupported practice tasks with cited booklet graph-selection types, retaining their locators and all unaffected content; no whole item was removed.
reviewSummary: All 15 practice items and nine quiz questions have correct qualitative answers and use booklet question types without introducing more advanced assessed methods; every quiz has exactly one correct option and specific distractor explanations. The theory agrees with the supplied teaching, and there are no worked examples or declared removals to review.
